node-1.label: A 35-year-old woman presented 11 weeks postpartum with right breast erythema and pain

node-2.label: Patient had three prior episodes of similar symptoms treated at outside hospitals, with the most recent occurring at 9 weeks postpartum

node-3.label: Medical history includes depression, previous treatment with cabergoline until 2016, normal first-trimester hormone levels, continued excessive milk expression despite weaning attempts, no recurrent headaches or visual changes, menstrual cycle not resumed, and current use of multivitamins

node-4.label: Physical examination revealed a 5 cm × 8 cm area of erythema and induration on the medial aspect of the right breast, no fluctuance, and easily expressed milky nonpurulent discharge from both breasts

why.why: Expert analyses from the laboratory physician and radiologist independently confirm that leukocytosis, elevated CRP, milk culture positive for Streptococcus agalactiae, and ultrasound without abscess are sufficient to establish lactational mastitis. The radiologist additionally notes the isolate is penicillin-susceptible, supporting targeted antibiotic therapy. Abscess and inflammatory breast cancer are effectively excluded, so confidence is raised from 0.85 to 0.9.

Continued milk expression and bilateral milky discharge still support milk stasis/engorgement as a secondary contributor, but expert analyses emphasize the penicillin-susceptible S. agalactiae infection and systemic inflammation as the dominant process. Confirmed infection makes isolated milk stasis/engorgement less likely, so confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.15.

Both the laboratory and radiology expert analyses explicitly state that ultrasound showing no abscess and physical examination showing no fluctuance exclude breast abscess. No new evidence supports abscess, so confidence is reduced from 0.02 to 0.01.

The radiologist confirms no focal lesion on ultrasound, and both expert analyses indicate that the imaging and laboratory findings exclude inflammatory breast cancer. Recurrent episodes, bilateral nonpurulent milky discharge, and lack of fluctuance are inconsistent with inflammatory breast cancer, so confidence is reduced from 0.02 to 0.01.
